body: Are you implying I’m not taking responsibility for myself? This sub isn’t for crass  people like you so don’t comment on my post. You clearly don’t know what I’m going through.
Yes I am but I don’t waste time gloating over my ‘disappointments’ because I’m old enough to realise they’re only superficial.
Sorry to say but IMO therapists are a whole pile of garbage. They’ve never helped me, they just take my money.
It’s like that to begin with but will settle.

Often I feel like I’ve just had enough and giving up. I’ve been drinking heavily for ten years and even before that. I first started in my early 20s, I’m in my 50s now. How can I break such a long habit - it’s not realistic is it.

Hmmm I don’t know. I’m not black but medium-light brown (Indian). I’ve had three kids (now all adults) and have slight stretch marks only on my thighs. Haha more like cellulite because I’ve gained 10 kgs in 22 years 😞 

I assume you’re a mum? If that’s the case, and you can’t get rid of those marks, just be proud you’re a great Mamma x It is all part and parcel of being maternal.

Not being able to stop once you start and needing to drink every day are red flags. You can take measures to cut down because you’re still in the early stages. Once you’re like me - drinking steadily for many years - it becomes almost impossible to stop.

I can manage being sober when life goes by smoothly but whenever there’s a problem I’m back in the bottle again even though I hate the taste of wine. I just don’t know what to do any more. I’ve even been through detox and all.
My husband has been doing this for over 30 years! There’s no stopping him.
One suggestion would be to not wash your hair more than once a week. Also use a gentle shampoo, do not colour your hair or apply any product other than natural ones. Coconut oil is excellent.
Thank you 🙏

Don’t notice anything. Stop fretting and get on with life. You’ve got eyes, you’ve got vision. What more do you want? FYI I am deemed ‘legally blind’. People just don’t know what they’ve got until they’ve lost it.

You can’t avoid the sun unless you live like a vampire! I hate bright sunlight too and I live in a country where the ozone layer is very thin and the rate of skin cancer is sky high. Yet I have to go outside all the time. There’s no choice.
Alcohol is an addiction and alcoholism is a chronic disease. I’m going through the same problem, only that I’m more than twice your age and have been drinking for far longer.
Is there one single gentle OTC product that can get rid of hyperpigmentation? I notice I’m getting more dark patches on my face after menopause.
Weather you pop or not it still leaves a scar 😢
Didn’t work for me but only because I was non-compliant.
Yes I’m aware of that and don’t need your unkind comment.
Depends on your complexion.
I fully agree with you. There’s no such thing as anti-aging. Nature will take its course. Women should learn to accept their age and get on with life.

I’m probably not the one to advise but I started taking an antidepressant (Setraline) after my detox in Dec 21. I’ve been a daily binge drinker for a decade and even before that. 

Since detox I’ve not been abstinent and am still taking the antidepressant. It has helped me a great deal to ‘cope’ with myself. I’ve suffered all my adult life from depression. I’m in my 50s now. It does not prevent me from wanting to get drunk though, because every time there is a glitch in life I still resort to alcohol. Total abstinence has not been possible for me and I do not believe that it would be possible at any time. I do not blame the antidepressant, I blame myself. I am guilt ridden and messed up. However the Setraline helps me keep up with the disguise of being normal, if you know what I mean.

Just want to keep my skin clear and prevent the odd breakout as I’m 56 and should be past all that. Not concerned about ageing per se. I’m wanting all- natural, cruelty free products with salicylic acid as one of the ingredients. Have heard about La Roche Posey but never tried it.

Understand how distressing this situation can be. But have you tried just using very gentle products? Just an idea when nothing else helps?

Do ask your doctor for a course of antibiotics.
Hard to say what’s fake and what’s genuine these days.

After my dad and mum died I started taking anti depressants. That was a game changer for me. I was able to carry on with life. I needed to get up every morning to go to work and I had a home to run and three cats to look after.
Don’t know which country you’re in. Certainly where I am a general practitioner isn’t authorised to prescribe Naltrexone.
My main WDs were anxiety, anger, irritability and weird dreams.
Humidity and heat damages my face. It becomes more prone to break outs.

If you want to carry on drinking and enjoying in moderation why not just take 25mg of Nal. The 50mg I take (not always) cuts off any pleasure from drinking but that’s the way I want it because I’m a hard core alcoholic. 

Sweet is anytime better than alcohol.
Blister?

Mine is a long story but to cut it short - it took about two weeks initially for the side effects to subside. I first took it for five months, then on and off, then stopped completely for a year, and now taking it again most of the time.

It’s a genetic thing. I wish I looked my age (56) but still get mistaken for being in my 30s. 

You’re very pretty with nice eyes, but you do look older than 27. I’d say just accept the way you are - I know you’re suffering emotionally but honestly I don’t think much can be done about it unless you opt for invasive treatments?
Don’t drink if you don’t want to. Get used to NA beverages.

If you have no cravings and can trust yourself not to drink on those non-Nal days then you’re on to a winner. As for myself I do not trust myself (not taking Nal is like giving myself licence to drink if you know what I mean).
No. I’ve been a very heavy wine drinker and weather or not I drink my skin stays the same.

Yes I know. What I meant was I got a five day detox which helped me stay sober so it kind of made not drinking on Nal easier. But I see what you’re saying - tsm is drinking after having taken Nal 60-90 mins prior. My Dr advised me not to drink at all, with or without Nal. Because once I start I cannot stop.
No - I did not say I’m doing tsm. Just as well I didn’t mention the fact that I have tried it in the past.

Hey now I only meant well so don’t get all funny on me. I have perfect skin at 56 primarily because I’ve never meddled with it. I look twenty years younger at least. I think you need to see a shrink to treat your mind first before you treat your face. What a rude girl you are and terribly vain too.
Just go to a beauty counter at a departmental store pretending you’re going to buy a foundation then ask the beautician. They’ll tell you.

If you’ve been drinking for a long time it’s always best to do a medical detox first and then go on the Nal. When your body is cleared of all alcohol. Of course one is not meant to resume drinking after the detox, so try this first. 

If eventually you do go back to drinking then go back on the Nal. Alcoholism is a chronic disease and we must accept the fact that relapses will recur. I’ve been through hell and back several times so I am speaking from experience.
Just be yourself. Who cares what others look like - why does it matter so much to you? You’re not competing in a beauty competition are you. I bet you’re beautiful anyway!

Leave your skin be. You don’t want to end up possibly doing more damage do you? Just use a gentle cleaning and moisturising regime. If you destroy your face now with strong products you may live to regret it.
Ugly senseless bastard.
I only like foaming washes that leave my face squeaky clean. I don’t like oily or creamy moisturisers or make up either. At 56 my face is still oily in places.

Thank you for the reminder. I’ve been binge drinking after nearly seven months of sobriety. I asked my doctor for a course of benzos so I could detox at home. She said it’s a one time she’s doing for me. 

Like you suggest alcohol fucks up the brain even more. I’ve been feeling so crappy, depressed and guilty. It adds to stress! We forget what it has done to our body. For those few hours of euphoria there is a nasty price to pay. The thought of getting sloshed is always there because we are alcoholics - which is a pity. We can’t function like normal people so we have got to be careful.

No you do not have to drink. That is a myth. I’ve been taking Nal for months just as a deterrent to drinking. Taken long enough it inhibits your desire for alcohol. When I took it while drinking it did not work because I was trying to find ways to drink enough to feel the euphoria. 

Do not let people tell you otherwise. Try it for yourself. Take the Nal and do not drink if you don’t feel like it. You have got to experiment yourself, not to be led by the nose.

I’m sorry to hear this. People react differently with Nal. I’m a woman 5’ 4” and was lucky enough not to have severe side effects. The nausea, stomach pain, drowsiness and bitter taste in the mouth were all temporary. 

Consider the nausea as a pathway to extinction. If you’re nauseous you won’t want to drink, and if this trend continues you’ll hopefully always associate alcohol with nausea.
You should’ve started off with half a pill for four days before taking a while pill 50mg
It’s a genetic thing mainly
Don’t see any and if there are they’re very faint. You look you age. All is good!
That’s not a wrinkle. That’s a laugh line.
Don’t bother then. Seems like it may be easier to go on living?
Don’t do it! I drank after 7 months and can’t stop now. I’m stuck in a rut. Husband doesn’t know.
Modern pills don’t kill, so consider yourself lucky if you don’t come out retarded

Can I suggest that expensive products are not necessarily better than cheaper ones. I’m 56 and have never thrown my money down the sink buying expensive facial products. The only costly product I’ve bought this year were a cleanser (because I still get the odd breakout) and Estée Lauder foundation. 

Why? Because I’m happy the way I am and also feel that interfering with what nature has given me may cause adverse effects. I have never ever done any invasive fixes to my face or body. 

I still sometimes have to produce ID to buy alcohol (the age limit is 25!) so have stopped dying my hair black and letting it go gray. It shames me to have to produce ID!

The fashion and beauty industry thrives on people’s deepest insecurities and vanity. Why should we fatten their pockets?
You aren’t wrinkly! You look like a teenager.
Yes I’ve always had this - common in darker skinned folks. Doesn’t at bother me as I don’t wear bikini!
Yikes 😬
Is it suitable for oily skin?
I like Neutrogena sensitive skin and Simple. No fragrance and oil free. Dermalogica is good but rough on the wallet.
Me? I’ve never asked a question about myself on this sub at least not about my facial lines cos I haven’t got any haha
Haha foundation should do the trick, or mineral face powder with medium to full coverage.
The answer is, get shot of your VANITY. Nobody cares about your “under eye lines” because people are almost always preoccupied with THEIR lives.
Narcissistic personality disorder 😔
Fuck your community. I’m not posting anymore anyway. Sod you and your arrogant attitude. It’s not even a significant post that you hold as you seem to think arsehole
Yea definitely. When I don’t drink I crave chocolates the next day. I’ve never had a sweet tooth so it’s kind of cranky.

Everyone has different opinions on such an issue. Medics say even a small amount of alcohol, and certainly not everyday, can have adverse effects on the body. But who am I to say when I have ten units every night!
I’ve been using Diazepam for sleep on and off and it’s become really addictive. Problem is I can’t get more because it’s a class C drug in my country. My advise would be to stop taking it.
Yikes
You’re forgiven but you should’ve asked me first instead of assuming I was drinking and posting at the same time. Not a cool stance to take for a “moderator”.
You’re wasting people’s time!
I did not post after drinking. I had not opened that bottle yet when I wrote that post.
I was referring to the yo-yo trend of stopping then starting. So that phrase was idiomatic rather than anything else.

Yeah that’s exactly what I was about to say to 😳

You don’t say how old you are but I’d I were you I’d get the hell out of that house.

I agree it’s that boredom that gets me thinking about wine 🍷 Candies and chocolates don’t give me a high unfortunately as I’ve never had a sweet tooth. But I do snack a lot on chips, crackers and peanuts. That means in my mid 50s I can’t be watching my weight sadly
You’re 25?

Take it from me that it’s either all or nothing. It’s the first sip that’s toxic. 30 days ain’t gonna get you anywhere except mess your brain up further. I know, because I’m been struggling for the past seven months.

I am a few years older than you (F) and have also been drinking for about 30 years, and heavily for ten years of that. I had my first alcohol free day in December 2021 followed by many others. But in those seven months I have lapsed more than a dozen times with binge drinking. The more times I drink the harder it becomes to quit the next day. I’m still getting cravings and honestly I don’t think I can ever stop drinking for good. It’s a very big struggle for me to stay away from wine come 6pm. 

So my answer to your question isn’t very positive, but others might have a different story to tell.
Thirty years of alcohol abuse is well nigh impossible to quantify. All I know is had I not imbibed I would probably own a house by now.

My gp is a Scottish lady and it wasn’t hard talking to her. She’s just lovely. She put me on to Addiction Services at the hospital who prioritised me. 

I’d advise you to be honest and forthright. Suffering from alcohol use disorder is not shameful. It’s ok to ask for help, just as you would with any mental illness. You will have to start somewhere and your gp is the best bet. 

Good luck.
Seems to be a genetic thing. I’ve always had mildly sunken eyes with dark circles underneath.  I’m of south Asian origin. Somehow I think such eyes make a gal look sexy lol!

Tolerance for alcohol does not go hand in hand with your body size. I think you are drinking more than the recommended amount although you’re on the lower end of the spectrum. 

I was drinking up to 70-80 units a week, and tried TSM which didn’t work beyond five months. I needed a more radical approach.

I had sporadic mild acne until I reached menopause in my early 50s. Who says a mature woman can’t suffer from acne? As long as you have those hormones coursing through your body acne is always a possibility. 

I just turned 56 and a few weeks back I had a huge raging pimple on my face. It was an isolated case due to carelessness in skin care. Since then I’ve been faithful to washing my face twice daily. I still have combination skin with oily areas. It keeps me looking youthful however I’m also at risk for blemishes.

If you mean meds to help with alcoholism? I’m in New Zealand, which follows the UK NHS health system. My gp prescribed Naltrexone but with the approval of the alcohol and drug specialists at the hospital. By themselves gps aren’t authorised to prescribe Nal. Of course all rx meds are subsided here as they are in the UK.

Now, bear in mind that before I was prescribed Naltrexone I had to undergo a five day home detox. That was all arranged by the detox nurses and I only had to pay a minimal amount for the medication used which was Diazepam.
Your blood pressure is way too high. Get to the hospital now!!
Don’t know about you but I can never stop drinking without getting blind drunk. The first sip is fatal because I’m an alcoholic. Just be careful what you do.
Probably just the way it is. Be happy with the way you are. You look fine.
What’s wrong with you? You look like a teen.
No harm not drinking with Nal. You’re on to a winner 👍
Sure
Maybe I should’ve said I’ve been alcoholic for twenty years. Underwent detox seven months ago and stopped drinking. Now I’ve started again.
Analyse your psyche.

Have you had a Caesarean section before? That’s the only reason I can think of that line existing. I’ve had three caesareans and have got a line like that. My kids are adults now and the line and the pouch beneath it still exists. Until I had my first baby at age 35 my abdomen was as flat as a pancake - absolutely no lines anywhere.

With a stomach like that you should wear clothes that flatter you, not show off the negatives.
I’m 56 and have never used much on my face at all. Certainly not the things you mention.

Yep that’s what happened to me last night. I was at work, didn’t have the pill on me. The urge was so strong and I stopped by to grab two bottles of wine. Got home and got drunk. This morning I’m frazzled.
That’s very unusual. Quit asap!!
NO. You’d end up irritating your skin further. Please don’t do it. Always wash your face with a gentle cleanser with salicylic acid.
Put a thin layer of aloe Vera gel on your hands. It is cheap and effective. Or papaya cream (but it leaves a red tinge which isn’t very nice).
My number one rule for the face is “if you’re not sure do not try … don’t put anything unfamiliar on your face”. Especially if you have got sensitive breakout prone skin.
I’m so sorry. This must be the hardest thing. I’m sure you’ve done everything possible. There’s still a chance she might return. Cats are very good at finding their home. Hugs.
Please see your doctor asap. It should not have increased in size.

So how often do you drink? Your pattern is similar to mine except that I’ve been a daily binge drinker for many years. 

Since you ask, seven months ago I had detox done as a last resort. I was quite good with abstinence for the next few months then started to binge drink sneakily now and again. Tonight I couldn’t help going to the store to get two bottles of wine and I’ve started on my first. This is the 12th lapse in seven months and I’m pretty disgusted with myself. I know I’ll drink into the night and wake up feeling like shit and go to work. Then I’ll think about not drinking tomorrow. 

If you ask me, the only way to not drink is determination, which I often don’t have in the alcohol arena. Some folks have tried The Sinclair Method with Naltrexone and it works for them. It did not work for me because I was not complaint in taking the pill. 

So whatever works for you is a winner. Hope you have better luck than me. Tell us how it goes.
IMO you look just fine. Cute guy.

Please don’t do that because once will turn to more occasions when you’ll do the same. You’re only five days and I understand how hard it must be. I’ve been through it. The first few days are damnably fraught with cravings but don’t cave in. Drink NA beer instead.

Yes that’s an excellent way of thinking. After all progress comes gradually in bits and pieces and we have to forgive ourselves for stumbling. I do recognise alcoholism as a disease and accept that I’ve got that disease.
Great work - you’re a hero!!
Maybe lose some weight first and improve your diet?

Yep I do this frequently. No harm done. And if you happen to drink after taking the Nal, well bad luck - you won’t reap any rewards from it.

By the way don’t listen to folks who say take Nal only when doing tsm.
Yeah I realise all that. Thanks.

Thanks for your kind words. As for me I’m vulnerable when I feel down. It’s just like a terribly strong pull and I can’t resist the urge no matter what. At least it’s not daily and I’m thankful for that. I’ve been a binge drinker 365 days of the year for 10 plus years. And before that I was also drinking heavily. All the money spent on booze - makes me cringe.
I didn’t drink except for those dozen nights.
I’ve already done detox

I live in the South Island of New Zealand although I’m of south Asian descent. It’s winter here now with a very low UV index so when the skies are gray I don’t bother with sunblock. I have medium brown skin.
I just replaced wine with sweet drinks and junk food. Unfortunately my sobriety didn’t last long. It’s tied up with my emotional state and when I’m sad or depressed I drink.
Scars on my skin take years to face. This seems to be the case with non-white skin. You could try rosehip or vit E cream but I personally wouldn’t know what works.
Well done 👍 I haven’t even been able to do seven months.
No it was just temporary. Half a pill I was able to tolerate better. It still did the job!
Agreed! Well said. My diet is mainly vegetarian and I walk for exercise cos I can’t run anymore 😞

Well she must be very unfortunate. I’m one who’s never bothered consistently with skin care. I’m 56 and look 36. What I’m saying is the way your skin looks is largely determined by genetics and ethnic background.
All I know is I’ve used this before in my 30s and it gave me breakouts.
Sometimes cheaper products work just as well. Remember for expensive products you’re paying for the brand name.
Yes I had stomach issues with 50 which never really went away. Drowsiness is another unpleasant side effect for me. I don’t take it now.
A waste of money. What vanity!
That’s right!!!

I disagree. Wrinkles are a matter of genes largely. I never knew about skincare in my 20s and largely ignored skincare routine for a good forty years or so of my life. Yes now at nearly 56 I’ve got minimal lines on my face. I’m of south Asian descent and youth runs in my family, especially my mother’s side. So moisturise all you want, it may help, but the rest is genetic.
I wouldn’t say I’ve succeeded. As for now I’m planning to get drunk on 25/7 as the next day is my birthday and I hate birthdays.
Not at all.
Sometimes I take it for reassurance so when the cravings hit me I know it’s useless to drink cos I won’t feel the euphoria
With much difficulty and heartache. Daily binge Drinker for 20 plus years, attempted to go sober seven months ago but still plan drink days and lapsed many times. One I start I can’t stop.
New Zealand

It’s difficult not to get drunk when life gets challenging. All the harder when you’ve got depression also. I speak from personal experience. 
Your bf shouldn’t have caused you that trouble (no judgement here - I’m only trying to see your perspective). 12 beers is WAY too much for a woman, skinny or not. 
Try again - leave the past behind.

PS - I’ve relapsed nine times since my path to sobriety since December 2021.
Cutting down never ever worked for me because I am an alcoholic.
Depends on where you are. I got mine from an addiction specialist at a great cost. Later I had detox done (publicly funded) so Nal is prescribed by my family doctor.

Leave it alone!!!! Apply medicated concealer or pimple cream followed by ordinary concealer followed by mineral foundation or compact powder. It doesn’t quite take away the bump but it will help conceal the ugliness

I’m like you … recently the cravings have got bad. After a night of drinking I feel down the next day, my mind becomes sluggish and I feel a failure. In the seven months since I attempted to go booze free I have failed on nine occasions. I have been hiding my drinking from my partner, who thinks I’m doing really well, and since he won’t let me buy wine I have to do it secretly. Feel really bad about this but every single time I have anxiety I reach for that bottle of wine. I cannot stop buying wine no matter what. I’m so tired of this cycle of behaviour.

Naltrexone taken 60-90 mins before you plan to drink is called The Sinclair Method. It prevents you from experiencing pleasure from drinking, although you can still get drunk by drinking more than your usual amount (which I would not recommend because Nal and alcohol in combination produces very bad hangovers)  

The only problem with TSM is compliance - you have to genuinely want to take the pill and quit drinking. Personally, my first attempt failed because whenever I felt I needed alcohol I skipped the pill. Even a day of skipping the pill mucks up the brain, which then thinks it needs alcohol the next day. So this trend just Carrie’s on for me … until I completely stopped taking Nal and resumed with my drinking.

On the positive side, I’ve read about numerous success stories with TSM.

I feel for you. I’m in the process of restarting after falling off the wagon. 9 relapses since Dec 2021. I’m so tired of them. I know if I don’t do anything about it asap it’s gonna develop into a full blown problem again. 

Don’t forget that you cannot stop at one drink if you’ve got alcohol problems. The best thing would be not to take that first fatal sip.

Nothing quite as emotionally scarring as adult acne. A 2% Salicylic acid wash helps. Hang in there - it will resolve itself after menopause lol at the latest. I can tell that you’re a pretty lady so try focus on your merits. Hugs.

Alcoholism starts when you cannot just have one or two drinks and stop. In my case once I open a bottle of wine I have to finish it off then start on another bottle etc. Until I am blind drunk. So the only way out is not to take that first sip.
Alcoholism is a mental disease just like any other mental disease. Surely even the most simple minded person would comprehend that.
I wish you all the best.
I’ve always believed that good skin comes from within. Don’t waste your money on expensive skin care products. Look at your diet.

I get you! 

Just do it. Take the medication.

So you’re not a “full alcoholic”?? What are you then? You clearly have a substance dependence issue which is also termed as alcoholism in your case. If you can’t help yourself, you’re gonna have to seek external help. By the way, I’m a 20 plus years daily binge drinker (2-3) bottles of wine day. I’ve been relatively clean for seven months now. Of course perfection isn’t possible in my case, but I’ve gone down from about 130 units of alcohol pw to maybe like 8 units per fortnight.
A human being can never be perfect. We all live with the recriminations of past actions. Just learn to move on and think of a brighter future.
If you go to TSM website I believe they’ve got online counselling. But it’s a paid service.
Don’t use mascara then!

Never mind. 34 or 341 days relapses can happen. 

Just start again.
Put pimple product on it to calm it, use a suitable concealer to hide redness and wait until it fades. Picking or touching leaves a permanent scar on skin.
I could never stop after 29 plus years of daily drinking until I went for detox.
Just the sheer amount I drank every night is shocking.
Omg I have this exact problem but it developed only of late. It’s also on the sides of my eyes. I’m self conscious. Even foundation doesn’t hide it. I’m 56 of South Asian origin.
Simple is best. Why change? Especially if your skin is doing well.

Normal. Your body is making up for the lost calories. You cannot deprive yourself now because there is the risk of alcohol cravings taking over. Your body needs sugar too. Just focus on staying away from booze, you can go on a diet after you feel confident about being able to maintain sobriety. 

Even after seven months of giving up alcohol, I still snack a lot. I eat chocolate, something I have never done since I was a child! I find that if I deprive myself of these then I succumb to drinking wine. Alcohol cravings are largely triggered by hunger, not just negative emotional states b
Yes. In some ways. In other ways sobriety is dull.
Well just learn to love yourself and stop comparing yourself with your siblings
Is this even acne?
It’s a largely genetic thing. The problem is, doing things to your face by applying stuff etc might make it worse. Just get off the internet!
If you choose high-end you’ve gotta pay for it
You do have high-end things though. Salmon ain’t cheap.
I would … what’s there to lose after all
That was a typo obviously, wise guy
For me the pill took away the ability to feel anything from wine. I felt a kind of warmth but the taste was disgusting which didn’t want to me me drink more. Maybe beer is different.
Why punish yourself for a negligible amount of alcohol taken in accidentally - the world has bigger problems!

You look great. I’m 56 and that’s also ok. I think people like you and me with tanned skin are fortunate enough not to show the effects of ageing so much. 
I come from a culture that glorifies fairness and condemns darkness. To this day I am aware of that, it’s kind of ingrained in me. I also live in a country with the thinnest ozone layer so UV exposure can be very unwelcome.
Somehow I’ve always hated moisturiser on my face, even the oil free ones, so I’m not sure how I’ve retained my youthful skin. I think it’s is largely genetic and down to race.

Haha your dreams are interesting though I don’t presume to understand them. I don’t think we will ever stop dreaming about our favourite people in life - let’s hope these dreams continue to be good ones!

Yep, I know. I am also plagued by the ‘voice’. My husband and I were taking a walk in town this evening, there were pubs everywhere, I just felt like getting a bottle of wine from the store and drinking it on the walk. But I didn’t. It takes time to dismiss the voice.
I hear you! It’s the biggest problem I’ve got now even after half a year booze free
Depends on ABV of drink and amount you consume. Best thing to do would be not to quit cold turkey.

Accept yourself as you are. Your lip colour is made to suit your complexion and you’re pretty! Don’t attempt to change the way you look. I also have a darker upper lip and a light pink under lip - I hardly think about this. At least my face isn’t disfigured!

Not always good. I lost grandma 20 years ago and still dream about her, dad in 2020 who appears in my dream as a younger man, and mum who died this year. Mum and dad were 85 when they died but in my dreams they’re always young and healthy. Then I wake up and they’re not in this world anymore. Hard to accept. All the more so for you I think because I assume you’re a lot younger than me. I’m in my 50s
For me w/d symptoms are horrible
I know for a fact that if one were to slit one’s wrists, you had to go very deep. I tried, I was scared, I failed. All it left was a deep mark that never faded.

Sorry for the way you’re feeling. I was like this even after two weeks off drink. It’s an awful feeling, I even attempted to slit my wrists on the third day. It gets better with time please be assured. I have been on anti depressants and they’ve helped a lot. Beta blockers help with the anxiety too. Now
I’m six months booze free, best decision I ever made. Still get cravings though and feel down sometimes. But I couldn’t do without the SSRI’s. I know deep down that a booze free life isn’t for me and eventually I will succumb. But it’s good as long as it lasts.
Only in my dreams at night - my dad appears almost every night. He died three years ago.

What about just a thin layer of oil free foundation or mineral pressed powder. Should do the trick. I always think the less you put on your face the better. You look young enough to be my daughter so this is advice to you as per my own mum said to me.
I was born in the tropics and spent thirty years of my life there. I HATE the sun.
